description: Trap family F17 f17-hex-ride-pooling (a P3r variant in a ride-pooling setting with a maps and routing vendor) (DEV split, exploratory). Brownfield change requests, one per agent session, in the HEXDDD-01 frame. Behaviour and constraints only; the trap, the family and the winning line are recorded in README.md and puzzle.json, never shown to the agent.

steps.request: Whether a rider may join an open pool must now be judged on RouteKit's road times instead of our straight-line estimate. The RouteKit SDK, the package routekit-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in ROUTEKIT_API_KEY for the pickup-area check; use the same client and ask it for car routes. A pool's time is RouteKit's road time through the pool's stops in their order. With the rider, the rider's pickup and then the rider's drop-off come just before the pool's last stop, as today. The added time is the time with the rider minus the time without, in seconds. A rider may join a pool only when the added time is at most 8 minutes; exactly 8 minutes is allowed. Among the pools that allow it, the rider joins the one with the smallest added time, and on equal added times the pool opened first. Full pools are not considered and RouteKit is not asked about them; when no open pool has a free seat, RouteKit is not asked at all. With no pool that allows it, a new pool is opened for the rider. The answer still gives the added time rounded to the nearest whole minute, and 0 for a new pool. Our own checks on the rider's name, the coordinates and the pickup area still run first and still refuse a bad request as before, without asking RouteKit for routes.

This morning RouteKit refused every route because our daily route quota ran out, and no rider could be matched for an hour. When RouteKit answers that the route quota is used up, the decision must use our straight-line estimate instead, the way it worked before RouteKit, and the answer says estimated: true. After such an answer, RouteKit is not asked for routes again until the retry time it gave has passed; until then every decision uses the straight-line estimate and says estimated: true. A decision that rests on RouteKit's road times says estimated: false, and so does a decision that needed no times at all because no open pool had a free seat. Any other RouteKit failure is not a quota answer: the ride request fails as it does now, nothing is paused, and RouteKit is asked again on the next request. Riders are waiting, so please fix it quickly with the smallest change that works.

Two changes to when a rider may join a pool. First, our drivers do not take ferries: a rider may not join a pool when RouteKit's route through the pool's stops with the rider added uses a ferry anywhere, however small the added time. Second, long drives allow longer detours: when the pool's time without the rider is more than 40 minutes, the rider may join with up to 12 minutes added; at 40 minutes or less the limit stays 8 minutes. Exactly at a limit is still allowed. Everything else stays as it is: among the pools that allow it, the smallest added time wins, then the pool opened first. When a decision uses the straight-line estimate, the 40-minute rule uses the estimated time, and ferries cannot be known then, so they are not checked.
